newsitem.title: USA: Dow staggers lower as Greenspan jitters hit market. [corrected 00:14 gmt 5/3]
newsitem.headline: Dow staggers lower as Greenspan jitters hit market. [corrected 00:14 gmt 5/3]

text.p: U.S. blue chips tumbled on Tuesday, as investors succumbed to a last-minute bout of nerves ahead of the second phase of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony.
The Dow industrials slid 66 points to close unofficially at 6853, with nearly all the decline coming in the last hour of trading.
The session was a dramatically mixed one, however, as New York Stock Exchange advancing issues outnumbered decliners and Nasdaq finished with a modest gain.
Evidence of the heightened tension appeared first in the bond market, analysts said, where the yield on the 30-year U.S. Treasury edged up to 6.87 percent from 6.83 percent.

"The stock market looked like it was just searching for direction," said Peggy Farley, chief executive at Amas Securities Inc. "It didn't have anything to make it go up and it had Greenspan to make it go down."

Greenspan, who tomorrow will complete his semi-annual economic report to Congress, put financial markets in a state of high alert last week with blunt warnings on stock prices and interest rates during the first phase of his testimony.
Many Wall Street analysts viewed the comments as an attempt to talk the market lower, and blue chips have declined with only a brief interruption since his appearance.
However, during an unrelated appearance today before the U.S. House of Representatives' Budget Committee, Greenspan denied his comments were aimed at affecting the market.
"That's not what I was intending to do," he told the House Budget Committee, later arguing he was incapable of affecting the fundamental course of the market.
"These are very thick, elaborate, international markets which are driven by decisions of millions of people," he said. "Nobody can affect them in a fundamental way."
Analysts remained unconvinced, however, noting Greenspan's finger still appears poised on a key trigger, the one governing interest rates.

"There's still some concern about what he plans to do," said Philip Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management. "He set the table last week for some pre-emptive action on interest rates."
Despite the broad sense of unease, several sectors showed signs of life as the market showed signs of a broad industry rotation.
Technology and energy shares, which had been under heavy pressure in recent weeks, were among the session's strongest performers.
Texaco Inc gained three to 101-3/4 to lead Dow advancers. Shares in drilling companies also firmed, among them Global Marine Inc, up 2-1/4 to 20 and Diamond Offshore Drilling Inc, up 5-3/4 to 61-1/8.

Among tech stocks, networkers attracted buyers after their extended sell-off. Ascend Communications Corp rose 3-15/16 to 58, U.S. Robotics Inc gained two to 57-3/8 and Cisco Systems Inc rose 1-1/2 to 55-3/4.
Drug shares were broadly weaker, as investors took profits in the shares. Merck and Co Inc fell 2-3/4 to 91-1/4 and Pfizer Inc slipped 2-1/2 to 90-1/8.
In individual issues, Tupperware Inc tumbled 8-1/4 to 35-7/8 after warning that its first quarter results would fall short of year-ago levels.
AmeriTrade Holding Corp jumped 4-1/2 to 19-1/2 in the discount securities broker's first day of trading following its initial public offering this morning.
The S&P 500 index fell 4.36 points (corrects from 4.37 points) to 790.95.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 6.19 points to 1317.37.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
